passages.title: Three wet nights in Snowdonia
passages.text:
Last summer my cousin Freya and I went camping in Snowdonia for three nights. Before that trip, neither of us (1) ____ ever slept in a tent, so we were very excited.

Unfortunately, it was pouring with rain when we reached the campsite. The tent was much smaller (2) ____ it looked in the photo online, and it took us ages to put it up in the wind. When we finally got inside, we realised it wasn't big (3) ____ for both of us and our bags, so we left them in the car.

That evening Freya discovered she had left (4) ____ own raincoat at home, so she had to borrow mine whenever she went outside. It was (5) ____ a cold night that we slept in our jumpers and woolly hats. Mud got everywhere, so we took (6) ____ our boots before climbing into the tent.

On the third morning, the sun came out. We dried everything on a fence, climbed a hill and had a picnic with amazing views across the valley. Looking back, the rain is the part we laugh about most, and we are already planning our next trip.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (1).
questions.explanation: "Before that trip, neither of us had ever slept in a tent": the past perfect (had + past participle 'slept') is needed for an experience before another past time. 'Has' is wrong because the story is in the past, and 'did' cannot go before 'slept'.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (2).
questions.explanation: After a comparative adjective we use 'than': "much smaller than it looked in the photo online".

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (3).
questions.explanation: 'Enough' comes after an adjective and is followed by 'for': "it wasn't big enough for both of us", so they "left them in the car". 'Too' and 'very' go before the adjective, not after it.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (4).
questions.explanation: 'Own' must follow a possessive adjective, and the raincoat belongs to Freya: "she had left her own raincoat at home". 'My' is impossible because she then had "to borrow mine".

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (5).
questions.explanation: The pattern is 'such + a + adjective + noun + that': "It was such a cold night that we slept in our jumpers". 'So' cannot go before 'a cold night' (we say 'so cold that').

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (6).
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'take off' means remove clothes or shoes: because "mud got everywhere", they "took off our boots before climbing into the tent".
